quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: Both halves look back at an unreal past — 'had known' and 'would have said' work as a pair.
quests.explanation: 'If' + unreal past condition (I had known earlier) + unreal past result (I would have said something). Third conditional imagines a different outcome for something already finished.
quests.textToSpeak: If I had known earlier, I would have said something.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The result leads this time, with the unreal past condition trailing after 'if'.
quests.explanation: Result ('she wouldn't have missed the flight') + 'if' + unreal past condition (traffic had been lighter). Third conditional can place the result before or after the 'if' clause.
quests.textToSpeak: She wouldn't have missed the flight if traffic had been lighter.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'We'd' contracts 'we had' smoothly inside the unreal condition.
quests.explanation: Result ('we could have avoided the fine') + 'if' + unreal past condition ('we'd paid on time', we had paid). Third conditional can use 'could have' instead of 'would have' for a possible past outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: We could have avoided the fine if we'd paid on time.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Might have' softens the result into a possibility rather than a certainty.
quests.explanation: 'If' + unreal past condition ('they'd hired more staff', they had hired) + possible result (the project might have finished sooner). 'Might have' shows a less certain imagined outcome.
quests.textToSpeak: If they'd hired more staff, the project might have finished sooner.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The possible result comes first here, and the unreal condition follows after 'if'.
quests.explanation: Possible result (I might have taken the job) + 'if' + unreal past condition (the salary had been higher). Reordering the clauses doesn't change the imagined meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: I might have taken the job if the salary had been higher.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Had' moves to the very front instead of 'if' — a more formal but still natural spoken pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Had' + subject (we) + past participle (known) + 'about the delay' + result (we would have left earlier). Dropping 'if' and inverting 'had' to the front is a natural alternative in third conditional sentences.
quests.textToSpeak: Had we known about the delay, we would have left earlier.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Curious about' leads into the embedded question, which keeps normal statement word order.
quests.explanation: 'I'm curious about' + 'why' + embedded clause (he changed his mind). Opinion phrases like 'curious about' commonly introduce embedded questions.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm curious about why he changed his mind.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Seems to know' softens the claim, and the embedded question follows without inversion.
quests.explanation: Subject (Nobody) + 'seems to know' + 'how' + embedded clause (the error happened). 'Seems to' plus a knowledge verb often introduces an embedded question about a past event.
quests.textToSpeak: Nobody seems to know how the error happened.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'It's unclear' leads into the embedded yes/no question with 'whether'.
quests.explanation: 'It's still unclear' + 'whether' + embedded clause (the merger will go ahead). 'Whether' introduces uncertainty about a future outcome, similar to 'if'.
quests.textToSpeak: It's still unclear whether the merger will go ahead.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Agree on' leads into the embedded question naming who the disagreement is about.
quests.explanation: Subject (The committee) + 'couldn't agree on' + 'who' + embedded clause (should lead the project). The embedded question here still functions as the object of 'agree on'.
quests.textToSpeak: The committee couldn't agree on who should lead the project.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Have no idea' is a common way to introduce a totally embedded, unanswered question.
quests.explanation: Subject (I) + 'have no idea' + 'what' + embedded clause (she meant by that comment). 'Have no idea' expresses complete uncertainty before an embedded question.
quests.textToSpeak: I have no idea what she meant by that comment.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Trying to figure out' leads into the embedded question, ending with the stranded preposition 'from'.
quests.explanation: 'We're still trying to figure out' + 'where' + embedded clause (the leak came from). The preposition 'from' stays stranded at the end, even inside an embedded question.
quests.textToSpeak: We're still trying to figure out where the leak came from.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: The whole subject, including its relative clause, comes before the main verb 'left'.
quests.explanation: Subject (The engineer who designed the original system) + verb (left) + object (the company) + time (last year). A long subject with a relative clause still takes just one main verb.
quests.textToSpeak: The engineer who designed the original system left the company last year.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Whose complaint went unanswered' explains why the customer reacted the way they did.
quests.explanation: Subject (A customer whose complaint went unanswered) + verb (posted) + object (a negative review). The relative clause here gives the reason behind the main action.
quests.textToSpeak: A customer whose complaint went unanswered posted a negative review.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: No relative pronoun appears here — 'the board had rejected twice' attaches directly to 'proposal'.
quests.explanation: Subject (A proposal the board had rejected twice, pronoun omitted) + verb (was) + adverb (finally) + past participle (reconsidered). Past perfect inside an omitted relative clause shows the rejections happened before the reconsideration.
quests.textToSpeak: A proposal the board had rejected twice was finally reconsidered.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: Commas signal that the clause simply adds detail — it doesn't identify which manager.
quests.explanation: Subject (My manager) + non-defining clause (', who rarely praises anyone,') + verb (complimented) + object (the report). Commas show the relative clause is extra, not essential information.
quests.textToSpeak: My manager, who rarely praises anyone, complimented the report.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Which' introduces extra detail about timing, set apart by commas on both sides.
quests.explanation: Subject (The new policy) + non-defining clause (', which takes effect next month,') + verb (affects) + object (all departments). 'Which' in a non-defining clause adds information without narrowing down the noun.
quests.textToSpeak: The new policy, which takes effect next month, affects all departments.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: The possessive clause gives background, but the sentence's main point is the discount.
quests.explanation: Subject (Our supplier) + non-defining clause (', whose prices rose recently,') + verb (offered) + object (a small discount). This background detail explains context without being the sentence's main focus.
quests.textToSpeak: Our supplier, whose prices rose recently, offered a small discount.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'Despite' introduces an obstacle that didn't actually change the outcome.
quests.explanation: 'Despite' + obstacle (the rain) + result (the ceremony went ahead as planned). 'Despite' is followed directly by a noun, not a full clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Despite the rain, the ceremony went ahead as planned.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'In spite of' means the same as 'despite', just using more words.
quests.explanation: 'In spite of' + obstacle (several warnings) + result (he ignored the risk). 'In spite of' and 'despite' are interchangeable, though 'in spite of' is slightly longer.
quests.textToSpeak: In spite of several warnings, he ignored the risk.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Regardless of' shows the result stays the same no matter what happens.
quests.explanation: 'Regardless of' + variable (the outcome) + result ('we'll learn something valuable'). 'Regardless of' means the following result doesn't depend on the variable mentioned.
quests.textToSpeak: Regardless of the outcome, we'll learn something valuable.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: Five pieces combine here: modal, negative, 'have', 'been', and the participle.
quests.explanation: Subject (The funding) + 'shouldn't have been' + past participle (cut) + degree (so drastically). This dense verb phrase expresses regret about a passive decision.
quests.textToSpeak: The funding shouldn't have been cut so drastically.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: 'Without a careful review' explains the missing condition that would have prevented the outcome.
quests.explanation: Subject (This error) + 'wouldn't have been' + past participle (caught) + 'without a careful review'. This shows a passive event that depended on a condition that didn't happen.
quests.textToSpeak: This error wouldn't have been caught without a careful review.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'Can't have been' expresses strong disbelief about a completed passive action.
quests.explanation: Subject (The proposal) + 'can't have been' + past participle (read) + adverb (very carefully). 'Can't have been' shows the speaker doesn't believe something happened properly.
quests.textToSpeak: The proposal can't have been read very carefully.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: 'It was...that' frames the whole sentence around a single emphasized detail.
quests.explanation: 'It was' + emphasized detail (the delay, not the cost) + 'that' + rest of clause (upset the client most). This cleft structure puts strong emphasis on exactly which detail mattered.
quests.textToSpeak: It was the delay, not the cost, that upset the client most.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: The opening clause builds anticipation before the key point arrives after 'is'.
quests.explanation: Subject ('What really matters here', a whole clause) + verb (is) + object ('how we respond', another embedded clause). Two clauses can link directly through 'is' for strong emphasis.
quests.textToSpeak: What really matters here is how we respond.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: 'It wasn't until...that' emphasizes exactly when something finally happened.
quests.explanation: 'It wasn't until' + time (Friday) + 'that' + result (we got any answers). This cleft structure highlights how late something occurred.
quests.textToSpeak: It wasn't until Friday that we got any answers.

quests.instruction: Snap the scrambled words back into the order you hear.
quests.hint: A relative clause sits inside the third conditional's unreal past condition.
quests.explanation: 'If' + unreal condition (the engineer who designed the system hadn't left, containing a relative clause) + possible result (the bug might have been caught sooner). Third conditional clauses can carry their own relative clause.
quests.textToSpeak: If the engineer who designed the system hadn't left, the bug might have been caught sooner.

quests.instruction: Listen closely, then rebuild the sentence in the order you hear it.
quests.hint: Three structures combine: a connector, an embedded clause, and a non-defining relative clause at the end.
quests.explanation: 'Despite' + embedded clause ('what he'd promised') + main clause (the deadline still wasn't met) + non-defining clause (', which frustrated everyone'). Several B2-level structures can naturally stack in one flowing sentence.
quests.textToSpeak: Despite what he'd promised, the deadline still wasn't met, which frustrated everyone.

quests.instruction: Put the scrambled words back in the order you hear them.
quests.hint: A cleft structure and an embedded question both appear in the same sentence.
quests.explanation: 'It was only after the meeting that' + main clause (we realized) + embedded clause (how serious the issue really was). This combines emphatic cleft structure with an embedded question for a natural, conversational close.
quests.textToSpeak: It was only after the meeting that we realized how serious the issue really was.
